fact: Maharashtra holds 2,696 of India's 6,628 specified dams, 40.7 per cent, on 9.4 per cent of the country's area (April 2025).
compare: India 6,628; second state Madhya Pradesh 1,370. Maharashtra has 9.4% of India's area and 9.1% of its people (projected, 1 Mar 2025).

stays_true: Counts change only when dams are completed or added to the register; the register is re-issued every few years (2023, then April 2025). The April 2025 figures stay true as dated. Next edition date not announced.
lead: 1,326 dams (1.97x) over Madhya Pradesh, 97% more
size_effect: Not a size effect: share of dams 40.7% against 9.4% of area and 9.1% of people; Madhya Pradesh has the same area share (9.4%) with half the dams.

The 2023 register (6,138 completed dams) could not be fetched from the publisher, so the lead is checked against the 2025 edition only.

compare: Maharashtra 46.789 BCM in 2,696 dams. Average per dam: Karnataka 133 million cubic metres, Maharashtra 17, India 50.

stays_true: Counts change only when dams are completed or added to the register; the register is re-issued every few years (2023, then April 2025). The April 2025 figures stay true as dated. Next edition date not announced.

fact: Maharashtra's National Highways grew from 6,249 km on 31 March 2014 to 18,462 km on 30 June 2025, third place to first.
compare: x2.95 in 11 years; India 91,287 to 146,342 km (x1.60). Now 12.6% of India's NH length on 9.4% of its area. Uttar Pradesh was first in 2014 (7,986 km) and is second now (12,123).
source: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, reply to Lok Sabha Starred Question 75, 24 July 2025, Annexure-I
stays_true: Both dates are fixed, so the statement stays true as dated. National Highway length keeps changing as roads are notified and built, so the 'now' position can change in the next Parliament answer.
lead: 6,339 km (1.52x) over Uttar Pradesh in 2025
size_effect: Rank rise is from growth: 2014 length 6,249 km was 6.8% of India's; 2025 length is 12.6%. Area share unchanged at 9.4%.
caution: National Highway length grows partly by notifying existing state roads as NHs: the same answer says about 54,004 km of state roads were notified as NHs since April 2014. Say 'length of notified National Highways', not 'new roads built'.

fact: Sikkim's National Highways grew almost fivefold, from 149 km on 31 March 2014 to 730 km on 30 June 2025.
compare: x4.90; next fastest Maharashtra x2.95, India x1.60. Sikkim now has 103 km of NH per 1,000 sq km against India's 44.5.
source: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, reply to Lok Sabha Starred Question 75, 24 July 2025, Annexure-I
stays_true: Both dates are fixed, so the statement stays true as dated. National Highway length keeps changing as roads are notified and built, so the 'now' position can change in the next Parliament answer.
lead: x4.90 against x2.95 for the next, Maharashtra (66% faster)
size_effect: A small base (149 km) makes the multiple large; the 2025 density (103 km per 1,000 sq km, area 7,096 sq km) is 2.3x India's. Do not claim Sikkim has the densest NHs: Nagaland (101) is within 3%.
caution: National Highway length grows partly by notifying existing state roads as NHs: the same answer says about 54,004 km of state roads were notified as NHs since April 2014. Say 'length of notified National Highways', not 'new roads built'. The increase is 581 km: small in absolute terms.

fact: West Bengal has 47 railway route km per 1,000 sq km, 2.2 times India's 21, the highest of any state (March 2024).
measure: Railway route km per 1,000 sq km of area
compare: India 21.0; Punjab 45.0, Bihar 42.0, Haryana 40.3. West Bengal 4,161 route km on 88,752 sq km.
source: Reserve Bank of India, Handbook of Statistics on Indian States 2024-25, Table 145 (data of the Ministry of Railways), 11 Dec 2025
stays_true: Route length changes slowly (a new line or a gauge change adds or removes a few km); the Handbook is annual (the 2025-26 edition will carry end-March 2025). Density ranks have held since 2020.
lead: 1.9 points (4.2%) over Punjab, the next state; in end-March 2020 it was 47.5 against Punjab's 45.0
size_effect: Rate per area, so state size is divided out. Delhi (127) and Chandigarh (140) are higher and Puducherry (46.9) is level with it: say 'highest of any state', not 'of any state or UT'.
caution: The Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 and Annual Statistical Statements 2024-25 give route length by zonal railway only, so the state split comes from the RBI Handbook, which prints the Ministry of Railways as its source. Area is ISFR 2023 geographical area (Forest Survey of India). Route km is the length of line open, not track km. The lead over Punjab is real but thin (4%).

fact: Rajasthan, India's largest state, has 17.9 railway route km per 1,000 sq km, below India's 21; Uttar Pradesh has 36.6 (March 2024).
measure: Railway route km per 1,000 sq km of area
compare: India 21.0; Uttar Pradesh 36.6 on 70% of Rajasthan's area. Rajasthan has 6,135 route km, 8.9% of India's, on 10.4% of its area.
source: Reserve Bank of India, Handbook of Statistics on Indian States 2024-25, Table 145 (data of the Ministry of Railways), 11 Dec 2025
stays_true: Route length changes slowly (a new line or a gauge change adds or removes a few km); the Handbook is annual (the 2025-26 edition will carry end-March 2025). Density ranks have held since 2020.
lead: Rajasthan's 342,239 sq km is 11% more than Madhya Pradesh's, the second-largest
size_effect: Rate per area, so size is divided out. In absolute length Rajasthan's 6,135 route km is the second longest network after Uttar Pradesh (8,823).
caution: The Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 and Annual Statistical Statements 2024-25 give route length by zonal railway only, so the state split comes from the RBI Handbook, which prints the Ministry of Railways as its source. Area is ISFR 2023 geographical area (Forest Survey of India). Route km is the length of line open, not track km. Much of Rajasthan's area is desert with low population; do not imply the state is neglected: the source gives no cause.

fact: Kerala had 1,050 km of railway route in March 2004 and 1,048 km in March 2024; India's network grew 9.4 per cent.
compare: India 63,221 km to 69,181 km (+5,960 km, +9.4%). Kerala still has 27.0 route km per 1,000 sq km against India's 21.0.
source: Reserve Bank of India, Handbook of Statistics on Indian States 2024-25, Table 145 (data of the Ministry of Railways), 11 Dec 2025
stays_true: Both dates are fixed so the statement stays true as dated; the end-March 2025 figure (next Handbook) could differ if a new line opens.
lead: Not a rank claim
size_effect: Not about size: Kerala's network is already dense (27.0 per 1,000 sq km, 1.3x India's), so there is little unserved area; the source gives no reason for the flat length.
caution: The Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 and Annual Statistical Statements 2024-25 give route length by zonal railway only, so the state split comes from the RBI Handbook, which prints the Ministry of Railways as its source. Area is ISFR 2023 geographical area (Forest Survey of India). Route km is the length of line open, not track km. Gauge conversion and doubling add track km, not route km, so route km can stay flat while the lines are upgraded.

stays_true: AISHE is annual; counts change when universities are established or registered, so the next report (2024-25) may differ. The ranking and numbers stay true as 'AISHE 2023-24'.

size_effect: Per million people Gujarat has 1.46 universities, Uttar Pradesh 0.43, India 0.91.
caution: The lead over Uttar Pradesh in 2023-24 is 3.9%: it clears the 3% rule narrowly and held in both editions. 65 of Gujarat's 107 are state private universities. Do not use with built-13 in one video.

stays_true: AISHE is annual; counts change when universities are established or registered, so the next report (2024-25) may differ. The ranking and numbers stay true as 'AISHE 2023-24'.

stays_true: AISHE is annual; counts change when universities are established or registered, so the next report (2024-25) may differ. The ranking and numbers stay true as 'AISHE 2023-24'.

size_effect: A rate per head of the college-age population, so state size is divided out.
caution: Of any state: Lakshadweep (60) and Puducherry (58, and 79 in 2022-23) are union territories; Puducherry was above Karnataka in 2022-23, so do not say 'state or UT'. The rate is AISHE's own, from its estimate of the 18-23 population.

fact: Karnataka has 4,529 colleges, just over half of Uttar Pradesh's 8,625, with 29 per cent of its people (AISHE 2023-24).
compare: Uttar Pradesh 8,625 colleges, 240 million people; Karnataka 69 million (projected, 1 Mar 2025). Per lakh aged 18-23: Karnataka 69, Uttar Pradesh 31.
source: Ministry of Education, Department of Higher Education: All India Survey on Higher Education 2023-24, Table 4 (page T-4)
stays_true: AISHE is annual; counts change when universities are established or registered, so the next report (2024-25) may differ. The ranking and numbers stay true as 'AISHE 2023-24'.
lead: Not a rank claim (Uttar Pradesh has the most colleges; Karnataka is third after Maharashtra in count)
size_effect: Karnataka has 53% of Uttar Pradesh's colleges and 29% of its people.

fact: Puducherry has 1,830 MBBS seats, 106 for every lakh people, against 7.9 for India (2024-25).
compare: India 7.9; next Andaman and Nicobar Islands 28.1, Telangana 22.1, Karnataka 18.0. Puducherry 9 colleges, projected population 1.72 million (1 Mar 2025).
source: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (National Medical Commission data), reply to Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 3054, 9 Aug 2024, Annexure
stays_true: MBBS seats are re-approved every year by the National Medical Commission and change with new colleges and seat increases, so the number will move; the very large gap to other states is unlikely to close. Treat the figure as 'in 2024-25'.
lead: 3.8x the next (Andaman and Nicobar Islands, a UT); 4.8x Telangana, the next state
size_effect: A rate per head. Small base: nine colleges.
caution: Seats change every year (the source says: 'Data for 2024-25 may vary on granting of permission by NMC'). Later Lok Sabha answers give Puducherry 1,873 seats (Aug 2025). Many Puducherry seats are in private colleges and serve students from other states, so seats per resident overstate local supply: the source does not break this down; do not claim doctors per patient.

fact: Kerala's postal circle has 5,062 post offices, one per 7.7 sq km, against one per 19.9 sq km for India (March 2025).
measure: Square km per post office (Kerala postal circle)
compare: India 19.92 sq km per post office (India Post prints 19.92). West Bengal 9.8, Bihar 10.1 (state area over the circle's post offices).
source: Department of Posts, reply to Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 4321, 18 Mar 2026, Annexure-I; India total and area per post office checked against India Post's Postal Network page (read 13 Oct 2026)
stays_true: Post office counts change slowly (new branch offices in 2023-24, a few mergers); the answer is for 31 March 2025.
lead: 1.27x: next densest single-state circle is West Bengal at 9.8 sq km per post office, so Kerala is 27% denser
size_effect: Rate per area. Postal circles are not the same as states: Kerala circle is taken as Kerala plus Lakshadweep (area added), which the answer does not state.
caution: CAUTION: the answer gives circles, not states, and does not say which states each circle covers. Delhi (2.9 sq km) is denser still. Needs the Department of Posts circle list before use.

fact: In April 2025 Telangana (16) and Andhra Pradesh (13) had 29 of India's 83 specified dams under construction.
compare: India 83; Madhya Pradesh 10, Chhattisgarh 9. Two states hold 35% of the total.
source: National Dam Safety Authority, Ministry of Jal Shakti: National Register of Specified Dams, April 2025 (summary table, page iv)
stays_true: Does NOT stay true: dams under construction are completed over the next years. Valid only as 'April 2025'.
lead: 3 over Andhra Pradesh (1.23x)
size_effect: Not a size effect: the two states have 8.4% of India's area (Telangana 3.4%, Andhra Pradesh 5.0%) but 34.9% of dams under construction.
caution: Weak for an evergreen bank: a construction count that will fall as dams finish. Telangana and Andhra Pradesh were one state until 2014; the register gives no reason for the concentration.
